posts.contentHtml:
Broken Tooth: What to Do Next in Weatherford, TX

A broken or chipped tooth can happen unexpectedly. You may notice a sharp edge, pain when biting, sensitivity to hot or cold temperatures, or a visible change in the tooth. Even when discomfort is mild, it is important to have the tooth evaluated because damage can affect more than the surface.

At F. Lee McLemore, DDS, patients in Weatherford can contact the office for guidance and schedule an evaluation. A dentist can examine the tooth, identify the extent of the damage, and explain the appropriate next step.

Common Signs of a Broken Tooth

A damaged tooth does not always look dramatic. Some cracks are difficult to see, and symptoms may come and go depending on how you bite or what you eat.

Possible signs include:

  • A chipped, cracked, or missing portion of a tooth
  • A rough or sharp edge
  • Pain or pressure when biting
  • Sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet foods and drinks
  • Tenderness around the tooth or gumline
  • A tooth that feels different when you close your bite

If you notice any of these changes, contact a dental office for advice and an evaluation.

What to Do After a Tooth Breaks

The steps you take after a tooth breaks can help protect your mouth and make you more comfortable until you are seen.

  1. Rinse gently with warm water. This can help clear food particles and keep the area clean.
  2. Save any broken pieces if possible. Place them in a clean container and bring them to your appointment.
  3. Avoid chewing on the affected side. This can reduce pressure on the damaged tooth.
  4. Use a cold compress on the outside of your face if there is swelling. Apply it in short intervals with a cloth between the compress and skin.
  5. Cover a sharp edge temporarily if needed. Dental wax may help protect your tongue or cheek; avoid attempting a permanent repair at home.
  6. Contact the dental office. Explain what happened, when it occurred, and whether you have pain, swelling, bleeding, or sensitivity.

Do not use household glue or attempt to reattach a tooth fragment yourself.

When to Seek Immediate Medical Help

Some symptoms require emergency medical attention rather than waiting for a dental appointment. Call 911 or seek emergency medical care immediately if you have:

  • Difficulty breathing or swallowing
  • Significant or rapidly worsening facial swelling
  • Bleeding that does not stop with firm pressure
  • A serious facial injury, loss of consciousness, or suspected jaw injury

For a broken tooth without these symptoms, contact the dental office promptly for guidance about the appropriate appointment timing.

Why a Broken Tooth Should Be Evaluated

Teeth do not repair themselves after a crack or fracture. A small chip may affect only the outer layer, while other breaks can extend deeper into the tooth.

A dental examination can help determine:

  • The location and extent of the damage
  • Whether the tooth has an exposed or irritated area
  • Whether the bite is placing pressure on the damaged tooth
  • Which restoration or next step may be appropriate

Prompt evaluation can help you understand your options and avoid putting additional force on a damaged tooth.

What Treatment May Involve

Treatment for a broken tooth depends on the amount of damage, the tooth’s location, your bite, and the health of the remaining tooth structure. After an exam, a dentist may discuss options such as smoothing a minor rough edge, a filling or bonding material, a crown, or referral for additional care when needed.

Not every broken tooth requires the same treatment. The purpose of an evaluation is to recommend care that fits the specific tooth and your oral-health needs.

Learn more about the practice’s general dentistry services.

Preventing Future Tooth Damage

Not every broken tooth can be prevented, but a few habits may reduce avoidable stress on teeth.

  • Avoid chewing ice, hard candy, pens, or other hard objects
  • Wear a properly fitted mouthguard for contact sports
  • Discuss clenching or grinding with your dentist
  • Keep up with routine dental exams and cleanings
  • Ask your dentist about changes in old fillings, crowns, or bite comfort

Routine visits can help identify wear, decay, and older restorations that may need attention.

Broken Tooth Care in Weatherford

If you have chipped, cracked, or broken a tooth, contact F. Lee McLemore, DDS for guidance and an evaluation. We can assess the affected tooth, answer your questions, and discuss appropriate treatment options based on your needs.

Contact our Weatherford dental office to schedule an appointment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a broken tooth always a dental emergency?

Not every broken tooth requires hospital emergency care, but it should be evaluated by a dentist. Contact the office for guidance, especially if you have pain, sensitivity, a sharp edge, swelling, or a noticeable change in your bite.

What should I do with a broken tooth fragment?

If you can find the fragment, place it in a clean container and bring it to your dental appointment. Do not attempt to glue it back onto the tooth.

Can I wait if a chipped tooth does not hurt?

A small chip may not be painful, but damage can still affect the tooth. Contact the office to ask whether an evaluation is recommended.

What if the broken tooth has a sharp edge?

Avoid chewing on that side. Dental wax may temporarily protect your tongue or cheek until you can receive guidance from a dental professional.

When should I seek emergency medical care?

Call 911 or seek emergency medical care for difficulty breathing or swallowing, significant facial swelling, bleeding that does not stop, or a serious facial or jaw injury.

posts.contentHtml:
How a Family Dentist Simplifies Dental Care in Weatherford, TX

Families often have different dental needs at different stages of life. A child may be learning healthy brushing habits, a teen may need ongoing preventive care, an adult may have a cavity or worn tooth, and an older family member may need help maintaining comfort and function.

A family dentist can provide a familiar place for routine dental care and help patients understand the next appropriate step for their oral health. At F. Lee McLemore, DDS, families in Weatherford can schedule an evaluation, discuss concerns, and receive recommendations based on each person’s needs.

What Is Family Dentistry?

Family dentistry is general dental care that serves patients across different stages of life. Rather than changing dental offices as family members grow older, many people prefer to establish care with a practice that can provide routine exams, cleanings, and treatment recommendations for a range of common dental needs.

A family-focused dental office can help patients stay connected to regular care and maintain a record of their dental history over time.

Dental Care Changes With Age

Oral health needs are not the same for everyone. Regular dental visits give patients an opportunity to ask questions, review changes, and receive individualized recommendations.

Children

Early dental visits can help children become familiar with the dental office and give parents an opportunity to discuss brushing, diet, and the development of their child’s teeth. A dentist can monitor growth and identify concerns that may need attention.

Teenagers

Teens can benefit from ongoing preventive care, especially as routines, diet, sports, and oral hygiene habits change. Routine exams allow a dentist to monitor dental development and discuss any concerns with the patient and parent or guardian.

Adults

Adults may need care for cavities, worn teeth, older restorations, gum concerns, or changes in comfort. Regular visits provide an opportunity to address concerns before they become more involved.

Older Adults

As people age, changes in health, medications, mobility, and oral comfort can affect dental needs. A dentist can help patients discuss dry mouth, existing dental work, changes in chewing comfort, and other oral-health concerns.

Benefits of a Familiar Dental Home

Choosing one office for routine dental care can make it easier for patients to build familiarity with the dental team and maintain a consistent record of their dental history.

A family dental home may help by providing:

  • A familiar care team for routine visits
  • Ongoing review of dental history and changes over time
  • Personalized recommendations based on a patient’s age and oral health
  • A convenient place to ask questions and discuss treatment options
  • Support for regular exams and cleanings

Availability and scheduling options vary, so contact the office directly to discuss appointment needs for your family.

The Role of Preventive Dental Care

Preventive care focuses on helping patients maintain their teeth and gums through regular exams, cleanings, and home-care guidance. During a visit, a dentist can look for signs of decay, gum concerns, wear, and other changes that may need attention.

At home, consistent brushing and cleaning between teeth are important parts of daily oral care. Routine dental visits complement those habits by giving patients a professional evaluation and an opportunity to discuss concerns.

Learn more about the practice’s general dentistry services.

When Should Your Family Schedule a Dental Visit?

It is a good idea to schedule a dental visit for routine care or whenever a family member has a concern such as tooth pain, sensitivity, a chipped tooth, bleeding gums, or a change in how their bite feels.

A dental evaluation can help identify the cause of a concern and determine the next appropriate step. If you are unsure whether a situation needs prompt attention, contact the office for guidance.

Dental Care for Families in Weatherford

At F. Lee McLemore, DDS, the goal is to provide clear, respectful dental guidance based on each patient’s needs. Whether your family is due for routine care or you have a specific concern to discuss, an appointment can help you understand your options.

Contact our Weatherford dental office to schedule an appointment.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a family dentist?

A family dentist provides general dental care for patients at different stages of life. This can include routine exams, cleanings, and evaluations for common dental concerns.

Can children and adults visit the same dental office?

Many general dental practices see patients of different ages. Contact the office to confirm whether it is appropriate for your family’s specific needs and to discuss scheduling.

How often should families visit the dentist?

The right visit schedule varies by patient. A dentist can recommend a recall schedule based on each person’s oral health, history, and current needs.

What should I bring to a family dental appointment?

Bring any requested insurance information, a list of current medications, relevant medical information, and questions you would like to discuss with the dental team.

What if someone in my family has a dental concern between checkups?

Contact the dental office and explain the symptoms or concern. The team can advise you about the appropriate next step and appointment timing.

posts.contentHtml:
Tooth-Colored Fillings in Weatherford, TX

If you have a cavity, a small chip, or an older filling that no longer looks or feels right, a tooth-colored filling may be an option. These composite restorations are selected to blend with nearby teeth, helping restore function while keeping the repair natural-looking.

At F. Lee McLemore, DDS, every filling recommendation begins with an exam. Your dentist can evaluate the tooth, explain the condition, and help determine whether a tooth-colored filling is appropriate for your needs.

What Are Tooth-Colored Fillings?

Tooth-colored fillings—also called composite fillings—are made from a durable resin material. The resin can be selected to coordinate with the shade of your surrounding teeth, then shaped and hardened directly on the prepared tooth.

Composite fillings may be used to:

  • Treat cavities
  • Repair small chips or worn areas
  • Restore minor tooth damage
  • Replace an older visible filling when clinically appropriate

They are a restorative treatment first, but their natural appearance can also make them a good option for visible areas of the smile.

Why Patients Choose Composite Fillings

Many patients choose composite fillings because they are designed to blend with the surrounding tooth. This can be especially helpful when treating a cavity or small area of damage that shows when you smile or speak.

Potential benefits include:

  • A natural-looking appearance
  • Shade selection to coordinate with nearby teeth
  • Direct placement and shaping on the tooth
  • A conservative option for certain cavities and minor repairs

The right material depends on the tooth, the size of the repair, the amount of healthy tooth structure remaining, and the pressure placed on the tooth when you bite.

What to Expect During Treatment

Your appointment starts with an exam and a discussion of the tooth being treated. If a composite filling is recommended, the affected area is prepared and the filling material is placed in layers.

The composite is hardened with a curing light, shaped, and polished. Your bite is checked before you leave so the restoration feels comfortable when you close your teeth together.

Treatment can vary based on the location of the tooth, the size of the repair, and your individual dental needs. If you have questions about your options, our general dentistry services can help you understand the next appropriate step.

Tooth-Colored Fillings vs. Metal Fillings

Both tooth-colored and metal fillings are used to restore teeth, but they differ in appearance. A dental exam is the best way to decide which material is suitable for a particular tooth.

Feature Tooth-Colored Composite Fillings Metal Fillings
Appearance Selected to blend with nearby teeth Metallic and more noticeable
Placement Placed, shaped, and hardened directly on the tooth Uses a metal restorative material
Suitable for every tooth? No—suitability depends on the tooth and repair No—suitability depends on the tooth and repair
Treatment decision Based on tooth structure, bite, location, and goals Based on tooth structure, bite, location, and goals

An old metal filling does not necessarily need to be replaced simply because of its appearance. Your dentist can evaluate whether it is functioning well and discuss replacement if there is a clinical reason to consider it.

Can Tooth-Colored Fillings Be Used on Back Teeth?

Composite fillings may be appropriate for some back teeth. Because molars handle greater chewing pressure, your dentist will evaluate the size and location of the cavity, remaining tooth structure, bite forces, and habits such as clenching or grinding.

If a tooth has more extensive damage, another type of restoration may be recommended. A personalized evaluation is the best way to determine which option is right for you.

How to Care for Tooth-Colored Fillings

Tooth-colored fillings need the same daily care as natural teeth. Consistent oral hygiene and regular exams allow your dentist to monitor the restoration and the surrounding tooth.

To help care for a composite filling:

  • Brush twice each day with fluoride toothpaste
  • Clean between teeth daily
  • Schedule routine dental checkups and cleanings
  • Avoid chewing ice, pens, or other hard objects
  • Tell your dentist if you clench or grind your teeth
  • Contact the office if you notice sensitivity, roughness, cracking, or a change in your bite

How long a filling lasts depends on factors such as its size and location, your bite, home care, diet, and grinding habits. Regular visits make it easier to identify concerns early.

When Cosmetic Dentistry May Help

Tooth-colored fillings can restore certain areas of damage while complementing the natural color of your smile. If you are also interested in treatments intended to improve the appearance of your teeth, explore our cosmetic dentistry services in Weatherford.

A consultation can help you understand which options may address your goals while supporting your oral health.

Schedule a Filling Evaluation in Weatherford

If you have a cavity, a chipped tooth, or a filling you would like evaluated, schedule an appointment with F. Lee McLemore, DDS. We will assess the tooth, answer your questions, and recommend care based on your needs.

Contact our Weatherford dental office to schedule an appointment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are tooth-colored fillings the same as composite fillings?

Yes. Tooth-colored fillings are commonly made from composite resin and can be selected to coordinate with the shade of nearby teeth.

Can a tooth-colored filling replace an old metal filling?

Sometimes. Whether replacement is appropriate depends on the condition of the existing filling, the health of the surrounding tooth, its location, and your bite.

Will a composite filling match my tooth?

Composite material is selected to blend with nearby teeth. The final appearance can depend on the natural color of the tooth, the size of the restoration, and where it is located.

Are tooth-colored fillings only for front teeth?

They may be used on front or back teeth when appropriate. Your dentist will consider the location of the tooth, the size of the repair, bite pressure, and the tooth’s overall condition.

How do I care for a composite filling?

Brush twice daily, clean between your teeth every day, attend regular dental visits, and avoid chewing hard objects. Let your dentist know if you grind your teeth or notice a change in the filling or your bite.
